entry.title: An audit that turns 1278 words into a shortlist of 83
entry.content:
An audit that turns 1278 words into a shortlist of 83

Meo asked for a cross-check of every gloss against a source. There is one on
disk -- 39968 Wiktionary headwords, cached in August -- and a script that prints
the course gloss beside the dictionary entry for all of them, which is the same
reading job the list already is.

audit_glosses.py does the mechanical half: it reports only the words whose gloss
shares no word with ANY sense the dictionary lists. 1278 taught words, 1176
supported, 19 absent from the dictionary, 83 flagged.

It is a smell and not a verdict, and the docstring says so in both directions. A
flagged gloss can be right -- the instruction TELLS the model to override an
entry that captured a homograph, so áo (listed 'Austria', means shirt) and súng
(listed 'water lily', means gun) flag by design. And an unflagged gloss can be
wrong: ý was glossed 'Italy' straight from senses that were about the proper
noun, so every error caused BY the dictionary agrees with it and is invisible
here.

The first run over-flagged badly and the fix is worth recording. My own stop-word
list held be, and, not, this and very -- so a gloss made entirely of stop words
had nothing left to compare and could never match. That flagged là ('to be'),
và ('and'), rất ('very') and every other function word, all of them agreeing
with the dictionary word for word. 96 became 83.

What survives at the top of the list shows the remaining limit plainly: tên,
glossed 'name', flags because the dictionary lists stork, egret and a childish
word for penis. tên means name. The dictionary is incomplete, and the tool
compares words rather than meanings.

entry.title: The cupboard candidate list, cleaned of its false positives
entry.content:
The cupboard candidate list, cleaned of its false positives

47 words in five groups, written to notes/CUPBOARD-CANDIDATES.md so it can be
read and marked up rather than living in a conversation.

Meo pulled ấm (warm) back: it was never a real candidate, only a false positive
of the keyword scan on the substring in "warm". So were kho (warehouse), cảnh
báo (warning), tiệc (party), điều tra (to investigate) and xuất sắc (excellent).
All six stay in the course, and the file says so, because a list of exclusions
without its own errors named is a list nobody can check.

The file leads with what it is not: a proposal, not a decision. Nothing has been
moved, every one of these words is still taught, and the cupboard mechanism in
0029 is not built.

Việt Nam and Tết are deliberately absent -- they are the course's own.

entry.title: Name the cupboard, and correct a glossary entry the evening made stale
entry.content:
Name the cupboard, and correct a glossary entry the evening made stale

Meo chose the name. It is in GLOSSARY.md section 3, Coined here, beside mute
stock -- which it must not be confused with, so the entry says the difference:

  mute stock    no gloss          the tutor does not know the word
  the cupboard  gloss, unqueued   it knows it, answers, never teaches it
  the course    gloss, queued     it teaches it

And mute stock's own definition was stale. It read "the 1,915 frequency-imported
words with no gloss written" -- that number is 0 as of tonight. The state still
exists and any future import lands in it, so the entry now says both: what it is,
and that it currently has no occupants.

0029 also gains a first pass over the 1125 glossed words, which finds about 55
cupboard candidates in five clean groups rather than scattered: places and proper
nouns, military, finance, state and administration, medical and technical. Việt
Nam and Tết stay -- they are the course's own.

Marked as a first pass and not a decision, because the same keyword scan caught
kho (warehouse), ấm (warm) and cảnh báo (warning) as military, all three on the
substring "war" -- the third substring bug of the day, after sword/word and
in/print.

Still not built. 0029 remains a proposition.

entry.title: The gloss list was missing the 221 items taught first
entry.content:
The gloss list was missing the 221 items taught first

Meo asked whether the list held every gloss in the course. It did not. It was
built from the frequency stock alone, so it left out all 221 hand-written items
-- 153 words, 46 rules, 22 sentences -- including tôi, tên, là and the address
and tone rules.

Those are the ones a learner meets in the first hours and the ones the course
drills hardest. They are also the ones whose glosses were rewritten this morning
under 0019. Leaving them out meant the review would have covered the back of the
course and skipped the front.

Now 1346 items in two parts. Part 1 is the hand-written items in TEACHING order
rather than by frequency, because that is the order a learner meets them in, and
it is marked read-these-first. It labels each item word, rule or sentence, with a
line explaining that a rule's gloss is a statement the tutor speaks rather than a
translation, since a reviewer would otherwise read a paragraph where they
expected a word. Part 2 is the bulk-glossed stock by frequency.

entry.title: A to-do list for the words, then the sentences
entry.content:
A to-do list for the words, then the sentences

Meo asked for one, focused on those two. Written to notes rather than said in a
conversation, ordered by dependency rather than importance -- a sentence built on
a wrong gloss is wrong twice, so the words come first.

Where the course stands after tonight:

  1278 words       done in quantity
    46 rules       all of them inside the first 221 items
    22 sentences   1% of the course, and 8 of them hand-written

The ratio is the finding. The reference course in METHOD.md spends most of its
time on assembly rather than on vocabulary, and this one inverted that in an
evening. Adding sentences until the number looks better is not the answer; what
a sentence is FOR at this size is a question first.

Nine tasks. The first is a Vietnamese speaker reading GLOSSES-TO-VALIDATE.md,
which nothing else can substitute for and which everything downstream inherits
the errors of.

entry.title: The gloss list for a native speaker, and propose 0030
entry.content:
The gloss list for a native speaker, and propose 0030

notes/GLOSSES-TO-VALIDATE.md: all 1125 glossed words in frequency order, with
the warning at the top and a note to watch for tone pairs, since nhắc glossed
'to lift' is the error no check in this project can catch.

And 0030, proposed not written. Meo asked whether there was a plan for how the
new words get introduced. There is not, and the sequencing shows why that
matters:

  items    0-221    167 words,  46 rules,  8 sentences
  items  221-1346  1111 words,   0 rules, 14 sentences

After item 221 the course stops teaching grammar and becomes a vocabulary drill
in frequency order. load_roster reads files in filename order, 90_frequency_
stock.toml sorts last, so everything glossed tonight arrives after everything
curated. That was correct while the stock was unglossed and held out by
is_teachable. Glossing it turned a staging area into the back half of the course
in one evening, without anyone choosing an order.

Not a bug and not a bad gloss -- every one of those words is wanted. The
proposition asks what has to be decided: whether they interleave or follow, what
carries the grammar across 1111 items, and what happens to the 54 candidate
sentences written when the course had 150 words.

entry.title: The shelf is empty, and the vocabulary in it is RAW AND UNVERIFIED
entry.content:
The shelf is empty, and the vocabulary in it is RAW AND UNVERIFIED

The last seventeen words. The frequency stock has no unglossed ordinary words
left. The course stands at 1346 teachable items, from 221 this morning.

READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE CONTENT. 1125 glosses were written by a model in
forty batches and kept or shelved by me, from dictionary senses and my own
Vietnamese. 540 words were shelved with a reason each; the rest are live and
will be taught to whoever runs this. NO NATIVE SPEAKER HAS READ ANY OF IT. The
one who sat a session that evening was never shown the list.

The errors found while doing it were not rare, and they are the measure of what
was probably missed:

  nhắc  glossed "to lift"       it means to remind
  nợ    glossed "to be willing" it is a debt
  nỗi   glossed "anger"         it is a classifier for feelings
  Đức   glossed "king"          it is Germany
  ý     glossed "Italy"         it is an idea
  cuộc  glossed "demonstration" it is an event classifier
  lương glossed "good"          it is a salary
  me    glossed "mother"        that is mẹ; me is a tamarind

Every one of those was caught by reading, not by a check. nhắc is the one that
should worry anyone: nhấc, one tone away, IS to lift, and _bare strips tones by
design, so no test in this repository can ever tell them apart.

Six checks stand between the model and the course and they catch SHAPE --
duplicate glosses, length, mixed kinds across a slash, a gloss giving away its
own answer, metalinguistic frames, descriptions instead of translations. Only a
person catches truth.

Written into notes/OPEN.md as section 0 rather than left in a commit message,
because a commit message is not read by the person who picks this up in a month.

The highest-value hour anyone can spend on this course now is a Vietnamese
speaker reading the glossed list.

entry.title: Twenty words after a pause, and the 403 was volume
entry.content:
Twenty words after a pause, and the 403 was volume

Zero batches failed, after two consecutive runs where all thirteen returned
403 "Access denied. Please check your network settings." A pause plus a
three-batch run instead of a thirteen-batch one, and it went straight through.

That confirms what a direct single call had already suggested: the block was not
the service being down and not the key. It was the rate of requests from one
address, and the right response to it was to stop asking rather than to keep
retrying -- which is the opposite of what a saturation would want.

Worth recording that I misread it for four messages. The log said "model
unavailable" up to batch 33 and "403 access denied" from batch 34, and I went on
counting failed batches and repeating that the service was oscillating without
reopening the message. The exact error was in the file the whole time.

Eleven of twenty kept. Six duplicates; thông was glossed "river", which is not
what it means -- a pine tree -- so the duplicate check caught it for the wrong
reason and was right anyway. lông shelved for "hair / fur / feathers", two nouns
across a slash the check cannot see; khớp and độc for being one spelling over
unrelated things.

entry.title: Thirtieth batch: 63 kept, and the slash check pays three times in one…
entry.content:
Thirtieth batch: 63 kept, and the slash check pays three times in one run

Fourth full window. A hundred words, 63 kept. The course reaches 1087 teachable
items.

The slash check caught three in one batch -- "to skip / ignore", "to update /
keep posted", "to arrange / organize" -- all verbs against non-verbs, which is
exactly the shape it was written for two batches ago. And it still cannot see
hầm as "basement / cellar" or khoa as "faculty / department", both nouns on
either side, which is the limitation recorded last batch as unfixable without
knowing what the words mean.

Four things that are not words: hoá is a suffix, the -ise of hiện đại hoá; g is
a letter of the alphabet; tí was glossed "Rat", the zodiac sign; sam is a
horseshoe crab, which nobody needs before a thousand other words. ả shelved as
archaic and faintly disdainful for an older woman.

Eighteen duplicate groups. Also shelved: nghiệm, phiên and sinh hoạt for being
bound or awkwardly glossed; Hoa Kỳ, Tây and bắc as place names, with Mỹ already
carrying America; dạo, lạc and hành for being one spelling over unrelated things
-- lạc is lost and also a peanut.

entry.title: Twenty-ninth batch: 67 kept, and the course passes a thousand
entry.content:
Twenty-ninth batch: 67 kept, and the course passes a thousand

Third full window in a row. A hundred words, 67 kept. The course reaches 1024
teachable items, from 221 when this evening started.

Eighteen duplicate groups, and three of them are the class that keeps
appearing -- English being the vague one, not Vietnamese. Each is a real
distinction Vietnamese draws and English collapses:

  cơm is cooked rice, lúa is the plant growing in the field
  đầy is a full container, no is full from eating
  mặc is to wear clothes, đeo is to wear a watch or glasses

All three are shelved under the duplicate rule and all three are worth
returning to, because the words are good and only the glosses collide.

bảo đảm was glossed "to sponsor" and means to guarantee -- which đảm bảo, the
same two syllables reversed, already carries. thức was glossed "delicacy (food)"
and means to stay awake.

u and New York were both caught by the self-name check: a letter of the alphabet
and a city abroad. Đà Nẵng shelved as a place name, the same call as Hồ Chí Minh.

Also shelved: đại, châu, tạm and khai for living inside longer words rather than
standing alone; lợi, trống and hạng for being one spelling over unrelated
things; thủ tướng and quy hoạch as institutional, with kế hoạch already carrying
plan.

entry.title: Twenty-eighth batch: 57 kept, and a check I promised and cannot write
entry.content:
Twenty-eighth batch: 57 kept, and a check I promised and cannot write

Second full window in a row. A hundred words, 57 kept. The course passes 956
teachable items.

TWENTY-SEVEN duplicate groups, up from nineteen last batch. The course crossed
700 glossed words between the two runs and the collision rate is simply
following the size of what is already taught. This check now removes more words
per batch than every other filter combined.

Last batch I said a semicolon-or-slash check was worth writing if the pattern
recurred. It recurred -- chùa as "temple / free", cao cấp as "high-class /
superior", tiếp cận as "to approach / to reach" -- and I cannot write it. The
existing slash check separates a verb from a non-verb, which is why it caught
"worthy / to deserve" and "to laugh / smile". These three have the same kind of
word on both sides, and telling them from "I / me" or "we / us" needs to know
what the words MEAN, not what shape they are. Recorded as refused rather than
shipped badly.

dính was caught by the length check instead, at seven words.

Also shelved: lái xe and mở cửa for being compositional -- lái, xe, mở and cửa
are all taught already -- and thi đấu for putting an adverb in a gloss; quốc
hội, trung ương, uỷ ban and bộ trưởng as institutions of state; đề, sát and cung
for being one spelling over unrelated things; Nhật, with Nhật Bản already
carrying Japan.

entry.title: Twenty-seventh batch: a full window, 69 kept, and 19 duplicate groups
entry.content:
Twenty-seventh batch: a full window, 69 kept, and 19 duplicate groups

Zero batches unavailable -- the first clean run in five. A hundred words landed,
69 kept. The course passes 899 teachable items.

NINETEEN duplicate groups, a record, and the reason is arithmetic rather than a
bad run: the course now holds 600-odd glossed words, so every newcomer has that
many chances to land on a meaning already taken. The check was added on a single
pair sixteen batches ago.

Three of them are English being the vague one rather than Vietnamese, which is
now a recognised class:

  cứu is to rescue, tiết kiệm is to economise      -- both "to save"
  bác sĩ is a physician, tiến sĩ holds a doctorate -- both "doctor"
  lĩnh vực is a field of study, bãi is a yard      -- both "field"

lương was glossed "good". It is a salary.

Two semicolon glosses offering a verb and a noun together -- liên hệ as "to
contact; relationship", điện tử as "electronic; electron" -- which the slash
check cannot see, and which is now the fourth batch to produce one. Worth a
check of its own if it happens again.

Also shelved: thơ for a gloss too specific to be spoken ("traditional Vietnamese
poetry"); Hồ Chí Minh as a city and a political name; tận and chuyên for living
inside other words rather than standing alone; bầu, phân, dịch, la and tướng for
being one spelling over unrelated things.
